title: Pickles, cucumber, dill or kosher dill

content.title: About
content.content: Pickles are fresh cucumbers that have been brined with dill, spices and sometimes garlic. The “kosher dill” version follows Jewish dietary laws. The product has a characteristic sour‑salty taste, crisp texture and a fragrant dill aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pickling cucumbers dates back to ancient Egypt as a way to preserve the harvest.
Dill contains essential oils that give the brine its aroma and have antibacterial properties.
Kosher dill is prepared without any non‑kosher ingredients and is popular in Jewish cuisine.
In Russia, “solyonye ogurtsy” often include horseradish, mustard seeds and redcurrant leaves.
Pickles contain more vitamin K than fresh cucumbers.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Cucumbers are virtually fat‑free and low in calories, making them suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains probiotics
items.content: Fermentation in the brine creates beneficial bacteria that support gut microbiota.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Dill and other spices add antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Hydration support
items.content: Cucumbers are over 90 % water, helping maintain proper hydration.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Excess salt can raise blood pressure; people with hypertension should limit portions.

items.title: Dill allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to dill or other spices in the brine.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improper storage can lead to growth of harmful bacteria, so observe expiration dates.

items.title: Added sugar in some recipes
items.content: Certain sweet pickling recipes contain sugar, increasing the calorie count.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pickles can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, sandwiches, burgers, or used in appetizers like tartares and cold soups. They are often served with mustard or sour cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the jar in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in a sealed container. Once opened, consume within 1‑2 weeks. Discard if you notice mold, off‑odors, or color changes.
